transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is I just feel worn down almost all the time. Like, even if I technically get a full night’s sleep, I wake up and it doesn’t really feel like I’ve recovered. I can get through work, because I have to, and then I come home and there’s the house stuff, clutter, little things that need attention, and by the time I’ve dealt with that I feel like there’s just nothing left in me for anything else. It’s not one dramatic thing exactly—it’s more like I’m running on low battery all the time, and it’s been hard to keep pretending that’s normal.
Do you find yourself feeling down or losing interest in things most days, and has this affected your ability to function at work or at home?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything obvious like that, it’s more this low, gray feeling that’s kind of running in the background all the time. I can still go to the lab, do what I’m supposed to do, talk to people, answer questions, get through the routines. So from the outside I probably look basically functional.

But I don’t really feel light about things anymore, if that makes sense. Even stuff I used to genuinely enjoy, like baking on a weekend or checking the telescope and getting that little spark of excitement, it just feels muted now. I’ll still do some of it sometimes, but it’s more like going through the motions than actually looking forward to it. At home especially, it’s like once the basic tasks are done, I don’t have much left for anything that would normally feel enjoyable.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. It’s not that I never do anything anymore, exactly, because I still sort of keep up appearances and I still make myself do things. But most days there’s this low, gray mood sitting in the background, and it changes how everything feels.

Like, I can go to the lab and talk to people and do what I need to do, and I probably seem normal enough. But inside I don’t really feel that… lift, I guess. I used to enjoy baking because it felt calming and kind of creative, and I used to get genuinely excited checking the telescope, even small things about it. Now those things feel flatter. I might still do them, but it’s more like, “Well, this is something I used to like,” rather than actually feeling much pleasure from it. It’s like the interest is there in memory, but not in the moment.
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or increased fatigue, even after resting or sleeping?

Yes. That’s honestly one of the main reasons I finally came in. I just feel worn down almost all the time, and it doesn’t seem to match what I’ve actually done, if that makes sense. Like, I can sleep through the night and technically get enough hours, but when I wake up I don’t feel restored. It’s more like I’m starting the day already at a deficit.

I can push myself through work because I have to, and I can deal with the basic things at home—the dishes, the clutter, the little tasks that pile up—but by the time I’ve done those things, there’s barely anything left in me. It’s not just normal “I had a busy day” tired. It feels like my energy runs out much faster than it should, and then I’m just sort of dragging myself through the rest.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I mean, “depressed” sounds so dramatic sometimes, and I can still function, so I second-guess whether that’s the right word. But most days, for most of the day, there’s this low, gray feeling in the background. It’s like it’s just running underneath everything.

I can still go to the lab, talk to people, answer emails, do the normal things I’m supposed to do, so I don’t think people would necessarily look at me and think anything is wrong. But internally, I don’t feel light. I don’t really get that little sense of excitement or ease that I used to get from things like baking or checking the telescope. It’s more like I remember that those things used to feel good, but now the feeling doesn’t really show up the same way.

So… yes, I’d say it’s there nearly every day. It’s just quiet and persistent more than anything.
Have you found yourself feeling worse about who you are or feeling like you’re not good enough, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day, no. I mean… I do have moments where I’m frustrated with myself, especially when I feel like I’m not as engaged or productive as I think I should be. I can get into this loop of thinking, “Why can’t I just do things the way I used to?” or “Other people seem to manage this better.”

But it doesn’t feel like a constant, deep belief that I’m worthless or not good enough as a person. It’s more situational, I guess. Like I can be hard on myself in specific moments, but I don’t walk around all day every day thinking I’m a failure. Mostly it’s more confusion or disappointment with how I’m feeling than a steady hatred of myself.
Can you recall if there have been days when nothing—absolutely nothing—felt enjoyable or gave you a sense of pleasure, even things you used to really like?

I’m not sure I can say “absolutely nothing,” no. That feels a little too strong for what I experience.

There are definitely days where things feel muted, like the volume is turned way down. If I bake something, for example, I might still like the smell or feel a small sense of satisfaction that I made it, but it’s not the same as really enjoying it in a full way. Or with the telescope, I can still recognize that it’s interesting or calming, but sometimes it feels more intellectual than pleasurable, if that makes sense.

But I don’t think I’ve had many days where literally nothing at all gave me any pleasure. It’s more that enjoyment feels harder to access, or it doesn’t last very long, rather than being completely absent.
Would you say that your low mood is present for most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's not intense or dramatic?

Yes… yes, I would say that. It’s not like I’m crying all day or unable to get out of bed or anything that obvious, which is partly why I sometimes hesitate to call it “depressed.” But if you’re asking whether it’s there most of the day, most days, then… yes.

It’s more like this low, gray layer underneath everything. I can still go to the lab, do my work, have conversations, look normal from the outside. But inside I don’t feel very light. There isn’t much of that easy little lift I used to get from things, like baking something or checking on the telescope. I can still do those things, and I can recognize that I used to enjoy them, but the feeling is just kind of dulled or distant.

So it’s not dramatic, exactly. It’s more persistent. Like background weather that doesn’t really clear.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I don’t think so, no. At least, not in any clear or significant way that I’ve noticed.

My appetite sort of fluctuates like anyone’s, I guess. Some days I’m less interested in food, especially if I’m distracted or just moving through the day on autopilot, but I still eat. And then other days I’ll snack more or eat something just because it’s there, but I wouldn’t say it feels like a major change.

As far as weight, I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting very differently or anything like that. I don’t weigh myself obsessively, so I can’t give you an exact number, but nothing has stood out to me as unexplained weight loss or gain. So… no, I don’t think appetite or weight has been one of the bigger changes for me.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still, more than you used to?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that in a clear way, honestly.

I don’t think anyone has said to me, “You’re moving slowly,” or “You seem agitated,” and I haven’t had that feeling of pacing around or being unable to sit still in a really obvious way. I can sit through work, or sit at my desk, or stay with a task if I need to.

Sometimes I do feel like I take longer to get started with things, but I don’t know if that’s my body moving slowly or more like… I’m just mentally sluggish or not very motivated. Like I might sit there before starting something, but once I’m up and doing it, I don’t think I’m physically slowed down in a noticeable way.

And I wouldn’t describe myself as restless exactly. Maybe fidgety once in a while, like anyone, but not more than I used to in a way that stands out. So I guess my answer is no, not really—not in terms of moving slowly or being unable to sit still.
Have you had any thoughts about death, dying, or ending your life?

I… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of having a plan or wanting to end my life. That’s not something I sit and think about doing.

Sometimes I’ll have more abstract thoughts, like… I’ll think about mortality, or about how exhausting it is that life just keeps requiring you to show up and do things, and I’ll feel tired of everything. But that feels different to me than actually wanting to die. It’s more like a bleak, philosophical thought, or a “I wish things felt easier” kind of thought, not “I’m going to hurt myself.”

I don’t want to be too vague, because I know that question matters. But no, I haven’t been making plans, I haven’t been thinking about ending my life, and I don’t feel like I’m in danger of doing something to myself.
Would you say that you’ve felt this low, gray mood for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. Most days it’s there for a lot of the day, even if I’m still functioning.

It’s not always like I’m actively crying or anything dramatic. It’s more like this low, gray mood running in the background. I can still go to the lab, I can talk to people, I can answer emails, I can do the things I’m supposed to do. But underneath it there’s this heaviness or flatness, like the color has been turned down on everything.

And it’s noticeable because things that used to feel a little lighter to me don’t really feel that way lately. Like baking used to be something I could look forward to, even if it was just making something simple. Or checking the telescope—there used to be this little spark of interest or excitement there. Now I still do things, but I don’t really get that lift from them. It’s more like I’m going through the motions.

So yes, for the past couple of weeks at least, I’d say most days have had that low feeling for most of the day. It’s mild enough that I can keep moving, but it’s… pretty constant.
